title: Readable Code, Architecture & Data Flow
description: Learn functions, modules, interfaces, dependencies, state ownership, asynchronous behavior, and maintainable changes.

lessons.title: Readable code and naming
lessons.principle: A clear name and limited responsibility reduce the effort required to understand and safely modify code.
lessons.practice: Prefer descriptive functions over abbreviations and remove duplicated sources of truth.

lessons.title: Use AI to simplify, not obscure
lessons.principle: Short code is not always simple code when it hides side effects or clever control flow.
lessons.practice: Ask AI to explain every new abstraction and reject one that has no concrete reuse or isolation benefit.

lessons.title: Functions and contracts
lessons.principle: A function contract specifies accepted input, returned output, errors, and observable side effects.
lessons.practice: Write a short contract before implementing state-changing functions.

lessons.title: Guard inputs at trust boundaries
lessons.principle: Validation requirements differ for internal helper arguments and untrusted external input.
lessons.practice: Validate network and form data before converting it to domain objects.

lessons.title: Modules and separation of concerns
lessons.principle: Modules should have cohesive responsibilities and narrow interfaces to limit coupling.
lessons.practice: Separate UI rendering, domain rules, persistence, and service requests for a simple task app.

lessons.title: Avoid cyclic dependencies
lessons.principle: Modules that import one another can create brittle initialization and hidden shared state.
lessons.practice: Sketch a dependency direction and refactor cycles before adding another import.

lessons.title: Data models and identifiers
lessons.principle: A data model describes entities, fields, relationships, and constraints across system boundaries.
lessons.practice: Model a task with id, title, done state, and timestamps.

lessons.title: Separate display from persistence
lessons.principle: Display ordering and formatting should not be stored as authoritative business identity.
lessons.practice: Use stable IDs for updates and compute labels or sorted views from stored task data.

lessons.title: State and source of truth
lessons.principle: State needs a clear authoritative owner; duplicated mutable copies become inconsistent.
lessons.practice: Identify which component or database owns each changing value.

lessons.title: Avoid stale derived state
lessons.principle: Totals, filtered lists, and labels can often be calculated from current primary state.
lessons.practice: Derive 'remaining tasks' from the task collection rather than writing both values independently.

lessons.title: Error handling and contracts
lessons.principle: Failures are part of a function or service interface and should be handled at an appropriate boundary.
lessons.practice: Differentiate expected validation errors from unexpected system faults.

lessons.title: Keep error information useful and safe
lessons.principle: Showing full stack traces to users may reveal implementation details while vague logs slow debugging.
lessons.practice: Return clear user-facing messages, log diagnostic context safely, and preserve causes for maintainers.

lessons.title: Asynchronous execution
lessons.principle: Promises and async functions represent work that may complete after the current call stack.
lessons.practice: Identify which operations need await and how pending UI should behave.

lessons.title: Do not report success early
lessons.principle: UI can claim a save succeeded even when persistence fails later.
lessons.practice: Await the actual storage or network confirmation before displaying a definitive success message.

lessons.title: Dependencies and change cost
lessons.principle: Each new package creates maintenance, supply-chain, and compatibility obligations.
lessons.practice: Prefer existing project utilities for a small use case unless benefits justify another library.

lessons.title: Review AI package suggestions
lessons.principle: A plausible-sounding package may be abandoned, unsafe, or unnecessary.
lessons.practice: Check publisher, version, license, usage, transitive dependencies, and maintained alternatives.

lessons.title: Refactoring versus behavior changes
lessons.principle: Refactoring should preserve externally observable behavior while improving internal design.
lessons.practice: Protect behavior with tests before moving or renaming logic.

lessons.title: Avoid mixed-purpose patches
lessons.principle: Combining a refactor with new features obscures the source of regressions.
lessons.practice: Split mechanical renaming from behavioral changes when practical and review each separately.

lessons.title: Architecture notes and handoff
lessons.principle: Decisions and invariants need concise documentation so later contributors and agents can preserve them.
lessons.practice: Record module boundaries, storage assumptions, and intentional tradeoffs.

lessons.title: Give future AI accurate context
lessons.principle: Short verified guidance is more useful than a stale dump of every file.
lessons.practice: Maintain a current architecture note and revise it whenever a fundamental contract changes.
